title: phase6e relevance harness — flexible expected-id matching pays off
content:
When the cortex-api `Snippet` response shape doesn't expose a stable `doc_id` field, hand-curating fixtures with synthetic ids (like `evt:cortex-Cortex-misc:01ABC`) becomes brittle — every chunker change rotates the hashes. The phase6e harness sidesteps this by building a multi-strategy matcher: try exact equality against the canonical composite id (`<repo>|<path>|<content_hash>`), then exact match on each individual snippet field (`repo`/`path`/`symbol`/`content_hash`/`collection`), and finally **substring match against `path`/`symbol` only**. The substring fallback lets curators write `"crates/cortex-api/src/strategies.rs"` once and have it match every chunk. We deliberately did NOT substring-match against snippet `text` to avoid accidental matches on arbitrary content.

A second pragmatic call: `/v1/status` doesn't expose per-backend (Vectorizer / Meili / Nexus) health today, only `indexed_repos`. Rather than hard-fail when the field is missing, the harness omits an intent bucket only when the query's `scope.repo` is missing from the snapshot, and records `omitted_intents` in the report. When `/v1/status` itself is unreachable, every intent gets omitted and the run still succeeds — the report just shows zero rows. This keeps the regression gate useful when one backend is down for unrelated reasons.
